cost: A search uses none of your plan's units: it runs backtests on the platform's own price history, no AI turns. Price: free for Pro owners.
what_it_does_not_do: It does not trade real money: every clone it starts is a paper bot, and going live always waits for your approval at the Trading desk.
It does not promise profit: most combinations are thrown out, and a clean result on past prices can still lose later.

It searches only stop-loss, take-profit and the entry threshold (a stricter, the same or a looser version of each bot model's own entry rule) on hourly bars of crypto markets; signal weights and AI confidence cannot be replayed yet, so it asks for them as IDEA approvals instead.

A winner is a proposal: on your Approve a winning long rule starts a blank paper bot on the paper long lane and a winning short (Red) rule starts one on the paper short lane (a simulated short at the live spot price, paper only), each trading that rule with the winning entry threshold, stop-loss and take-profit. Nothing starts before you approve. On your Approve a Flash finding runs as a paper test on the paper Flash lane (the lab applies it to the 5-minute bars that close afterwards: no bot, no order). The lab starts paper bots only, never one on your own exchange or with real money.

It does not know which market comes next: a bear bot is a bet on a falling market and a bull bot on a rising one, and the market read beside a winner is information about the past, not a forecast. A paper result is an edge on past prices, never what a live table would pay.

It learns from earlier runs only in these ways: a setup that failed the blind test is not blind-tested again for 36 days, a model/market pair with blind-test failures is ranked lower and one never blind-tested is ranked higher, each run adds stop-loss/take-profit settings it has never tried, and a setup's score counts its trades in the market regime (trend up, trend down or range) read at the end of the search period. It does not train a model on past results.

It judges a setup only on windows the choice never saw, on a fixed grid (7 days for long term, 1 or 5 hours for Flash), each labelled rising, falling or range by its coin: more than half of the windows of its kind must make money, the pooled result must clear the bar once and it needs at least 20 closed trades. Searches finished before 12 Nov used four 36-day windows and keep their results.

It replays skills and Named Combinations as candle rules in the replay's own grammar (a majority vote of a combination's models); a skill whose live signal needs what candles do not hold is listed as not replayable, with the reason.
It does not read news, social posts or order books, and it does not build new markets or backtest setups itself.
It is not Build a Company's product: it is EventTrader's own Quant Lab.
can_tune: Stop-loss: three levels around each bot model's own (0.6x, 1x and 1.6x, kept between 1% and 20%).
Entry threshold: each model's entry rule stricter, as it is, or looser (new 2026-10-28).
Which bot model: all 16 models with a backtest set-up (7 of them equip as free paper bots).
Which market: 12 crypto markets (BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, ADA, DOGE, AVAX, LINK, LTC, DOT, ATOM) on hourly bars.

cannot_tune.why: none of the 16 replayed bot models has weights (each decides by rules where every condition must hold), so a scored version of each model has to be built and replayed first.
cannot_tune.line: Needs a large build: none of the 16 replayed bot models has weights (each decides by rules where every condition must hold), so a scored version of each model has to be built and replayed first.

cannot_tune.why: the replayed bot models give no confidence number and the replay's confidence hook is reserved but unused, so a new replay for the 5-minute strategies that do have one is needed.

cannot_tune.what: Position size and number of open positions
cannot_tune.why: the set-ups carry both and the replay accepts a max-positions override; the search does not vary them yet.

cannot_tune.what: Indicator periods (for example RSI 14 to RSI 10)
cannot_tune.why: indicators are named in each set-up (RSI_14, EMA_21 ...); the search would have to rewrite them and the rules together.
cannot_tune.line: Needs a medium build: indicators are named in each set-up (RSI_14, EMA_21 ...); the search would have to rewrite them and the rules together.

cannot_tune.what: Cross-exchange arbitrage, funding-rate carry, DEX replay
cannot_tune.why: their own engines exist (spreads, funding rates, DEX data) but run on a live window, not on the search's walk-forward split with a held-back period; each needs a windowed replay.

cannot_tune.why: none of these is part of the replayed history.

what_changed.text: The search now learns from earlier runs: a setup that failed the blind test is not blind-tested again for 36 days, pairs that failed are ranked lower and untested pairs higher, each run adds settings never tried, and the score counts the market regime (trend up, down or range) at the end of the search period.

A search now starts with two questions, horizon (Flash 1 hour, Flash 5 hours, long term) and risk (low or high). Every held-back window is labelled rising, falling or range by its own coin, a winner is all-weather, bear or bull, and short rules are searched like long ones. A short (Red) winner starts on the paper short lane: a simulated short at the live spot price, paper only. Flash searches 5-minute bars of BTC and ETH.

A winner now starts a blank paper bot that trades the winning rule itself with the winning entry threshold, stop-loss and take-profit, for every long rule (free, paid and Blue; the lab never buys a model). Short (Red) rules had no lane then; since 2026-11-12 they run on the paper short lane.
The Quant Lab page now lists in one place what the lab can tune today and what it cannot, with the size of the build each missing piece would need.

The lab now checks an idea against what the platform really has before it asks you to approve it, and every idea card says whether it exists today, needs a small, medium or large build, or is not possible, and why.

tried_counting: TRIED counts every combination a FINISHED search replayed; a failed search's rows are removed. A re-test of a known setup on newer prices is a try: it can be shortlisted, so it raises the bar.

method.search_period: 54 days of hourly bars before each held-back window (its own)
method.held_back: at least 4 windows of 36 days on a fixed grid, never overlapping, holding both a falling and a rising market; the search never sees them
method.pass: money made (net of fee and slippage) on at least three quarters of the windows, the pooled result over all windows above the bar, and at least 20 closed trades; a bot that never trades cannot pass
method.bar: one-sided 5% test split over every combination tried, applied once to the pooled result; never below 1%

profiles.kinds: Every held-back window is labelled by what its coin did in it: rising, falling or range. A setup can pass as an all-weather bot (every window, and money in both falling and rising ones), a bear bot (falling windows only) or a bull bot (rising windows only). Short rules are searched like long ones.
profiles.pass: Judged only on windows the choice never saw. It needs at least 12 unseen WINDOWS of its kind for long term (7-day windows) and at least 100 unseen windows of its kind for Flash (1-hour or 5-hour windows): these are counts of windows, not of trades. It passes if, net of fees, it made money on more than half of those windows, its pooled result clears the bar once (every combination ever tried counts, times three for the three kinds) and it closed at least 20 trades in total across them (for Flash too: 20 trades, not 100). A long-term window under 5 trades does not count; a Flash window always counts, and one under the volume floor counts as a loss.

risk.low: no held-back window of any kind below -15%

profiles.range_band: a 7-day move inside +/-2% is a range; shorter windows scale by the square root of time
profiles.edge: A paper result is an edge measured on past prices, not what a live table would pay: a paper round pays a fixed 2x, a live one shares the pool.
profiles.read: The market read beside a winner is the coin's latest complete window and how often that read was followed by the same kind before: information about the past, not a forecast.
